verdicts.tldr: Index recomputes the same slug expression three times per row; one `dir` local carries it
verdicts.details: comment.go:175-176 holds three byte-identical copies of strings.TrimPrefix(path.Dir(urlToFile(u)), "/"), one for the <li> href and two for the source and help hrefs, with nothing tying them together: an edit to the slug rule that misses a copy points a row's source link at a different directory than its page link, and the landing page is the only navigation a reviewer has. The isolated rewrite renders byte-identically. It saves no lines, 196 -> 196 for the file and 4 -> 4 for the statement, so the candidate's "5 lines to 4" is off; the gain is one name, not shorter code. Fix: hoist dir := strings.TrimPrefix(path.Dir(urlToFile(u)), "/") above the Sprintf and pass dir, u, dir, dir.

verdicts.tldr: the `direct` map exists only to answer a membership test contains answers in place
verdicts.details: comment.go:56-59 allocates and fills direct in the default branch, and it is read at one site, comment.go:69 !direct[r]. contains(p.ChangedRealms, r), already in the package at plan.go:335 and already used by isSeed, says the same thing in the line that asks, and the map with its loop goes: 196 -> 192. Two of the candidate's qualifications are loose and neither changes the call: the map sits inside the default case, so the gnoweb branch never builds it, and the single read site executes once per p.Realms entry rather than once. The scan is bounded by -max-realms (defaultMaxRealms 25, main.go:29) but that flag documents 0 as no cap, so the trade is len(Realms)*len(ChangedRealms) string compares once per preview build against one map allocation. Fix: delete lines 56-59 and read if !contains(p.ChangedRealms, r) && !isSeed(r, p).

verdicts.tldr: the marker and the heading are built into b above the guard that discards them
verdicts.details: comment.go:19-20 write CommentMarker and the "### gnoweb preview" heading into b, and comment.go:24 if p.Empty() { return "" } throws the builder away. Empty() is !p.Gnoweb && len(p.Realms) == 0 (plan.go:91) and reads nothing the two writes touch, so the reorder is free. The waste is two short appends; what the reader loses is that the function reads as if the marker always leads the body when the body can still be empty, and the marker is what the publishing job matches to update the sticky comment in place, so a later edit returning b.String() from the guard would post and then keep a marker-only comment. No line change: 196 -> 196. Fix: move the three-line guard above var b strings.Builder.
